column1: # SUPER -- docs/design/SUPER.0.md: super(x) answers the immediate
# parent type of its argument, structurally. The scalar and kind
# ladders are pinned where they always were (number-model.tsv,
# number-tower.tsv, edge.tsv); this file pins the structural rules
# that replaced the old blanket `top`: maps and lists lift child by
# child (shape -- optionality, closedness, spread -- carried, the
# spread template lifted), preferences unwrap to their value's
# parent, disjunctions distribute arm by arm (top absorbs, duplicates
# collapse), constraints answer the kind they constrain (absorbed
# leaf kind, else comparison domain, else top for the multi-domain
# length()), and a recursion residual stays a symbolic call -- the
# finite spelling of a lift that is itself recursive.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# --- maps and lists: descend, carry shape, lift the spread ---
super-map-canon
super-map-spread-canon
super-map-empty-canon
super-list-canon
super-list-empty-canon
super-ref-map-canon
super-type-def-canon
super-ladder-map-canon
# --- the lift is a usable schema: admits at the lifted level ---
super-map-as-schema-gens
super-map-as-schema-errc
# --- preferences unwrap: softness does not survive typing ---
super-pref-canon
super-pref-kind-canon
# --- disjunctions distribute; top absorbs; duplicates collapse ---
super-disjunct-canon
super-disjunct-mixed-canon
super-disjunct-kinds-canon
super-ranked-disjunct-canon
# --- constraints answer the kind they constrain ---
super-constraint-number-canon
super-constraint-string-canon
super-constraint-re-canon
super-constraint-kind-canon
super-constraint-length-canon
# --- shape carries: closedness survives the lift, and the lifted
# spread admits at the lifted level (floats the original refused)
super-closed-carried-errc
super-list-spread-canon
super-list-spread-admits-gens
# --- recursion stays symbolic: the finite spelling of a recursive
# lift, direct or met during descent (SUPER.0.md, the phase boundary)
super-recursive-symbolic-canon
super-descent-residual-canon
# --- the null ladder: the null KIND prints as the value does, and
# its own parent is top (the print ambiguity is recorded in SUPER.0.md)
super-null-kind-canon
super-null-ladder-canon
# --- the whole kind ladder, in one row, because a FIGURE draws it ---
# `aontu view lattice` draws this ladder as the value lattice: `top`
# at the join, the kind families under it, `path()` under `string`,
# the four numeric leaves under `number`. The figure carries its own
# copy of the shape (the tables in ts/src/view.ts and
# go/view_lattice.go), so this row is where the two are held together
# -- change the ladder and this fails, which is the reminder that the
# figure has to grow or lose a node with it.
super-kind-ladder-canon
column3:
string: super(string)
path: super(path())
number: super(number)
integer: super(integer)
float: super(float)
biginteger: super(biginteger)
bigdecimal: super(bigdecimal)
boolean: super(boolean)
null: super(super(null))
